note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names. Empty fields (track, code, level, description) are filled; authored transfer_check values replace ONLY the two known generic placeholder sentences — real source checks are never overwritten (guard in tools/normalize_blocks.py).

themes.description: Marking out and measuring before cutting — the discipline that decides whether parts fit.
themes.transfer_check: Mark out and cut a piece to a stated dimension within tolerance, showing the marking before the cut.

themes.description: Joining two pieces of wood so they stay joined — the basic joints and choosing between them.
themes.transfer_check: Make one wood joint that holds under load, and name where you would use it and where you would not.

themes.description: Hacksaw, snips and files — cutting and finishing metal safely at the bench.
themes.transfer_check: Cut and file a piece of metal to a line safely, finishing the edge so it passes a finger test.

themes.description: The stitches and seams that survive washing and wearing — sewing as construction, not decoration.
themes.transfer_check: Sew one seam and one fastening that survive a wash and a pull test, by hand or machine.

themes.description: Mixing, forming and curing — the wet materials that become permanent, and the timing that governs them.
themes.transfer_check: Mix and form one small piece in clay or concrete with correct proportions, and cure it to a sound result.

themes.description: The working drawing — dimensions, views, materials list — good enough that someone else could build it.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a dimensioned working drawing with a materials list that another maker builds from without asking you anything.

themes.description: Sanding, sealing, painting and edges — the last ten percent that makes a made thing look meant.
themes.transfer_check: Take one made piece through sanding, sealing or painting to a finish somebody would put in their home.

themes.description: Building to a real person's need and measurements, checked with them before, during and after.
themes.transfer_check: Build one object to a real person's stated need and measurements, checked with them before, during, and at handover.

themes.description: Reading a failure for its lesson — what broke, why, and the change the next version carries.
themes.transfer_check: Break or find the failure in a prototype, diagnose why, and show the change the next version carries.

themes.description: Materials, time and overhead totalled honestly — what the thing actually cost to make.
themes.transfer_check: Cost one real made object honestly — materials, time, overhead — and state the price it would need to be worth making.

themes.description: The questions and checks that find a fault before a screwdriver moves — symptom, history, most likely cause.
themes.transfer_check: Diagnose one real fault to a most-likely cause using questions and checks alone, before any tool touches it.

themes.theme: The four repairs every household needs (RP)
themes.description: The repeating household repairs — leaks, sticking, wobbles, blockages — mastered as standard procedures.
themes.transfer_check: Complete two of the four standard household repairs on real faults, following the taught procedure.

themes.description: Buttons, hems, tears and zips — the clothing repairs that keep garments in service for years.
themes.transfer_check: Repair a real garment — button, hem, tear or zip — so the repair survives a wash and the garment returns to use.

themes.description: The small engine's usual failures — fuel, spark, air — diagnosed in order on a real machine.
themes.transfer_check: Work the fuel-spark-air sequence on a real non-starting small engine and get it running or isolate the failed system.

themes.description: The electronic repairs still open to a careful amateur — connections, batteries, switches — and the line where danger starts.
themes.transfer_check: Complete one safe electronics repair — connection, battery, switch — and state exactly where the amateur line is and why.

themes.description: Loose joints, broken legs and worn surfaces — bringing real furniture back to use.
themes.transfer_check: Bring one real piece of furniture back to use — joint, leg or surface — with before and after evidence.

themes.description: The bicycle as the repairable machine — punctures, brakes and gears serviced with basic tools.
themes.transfer_check: Fix a real puncture and adjust brakes or gears to a working standard, then ride the result.

themes.description: Repair cafés and fix-it events — repairing in public so the skill and the habit spread.
themes.transfer_check: Take part in or stage a repair event: fix one item in front of others and talk one person through what you did.

themes.description: Judging repair against replacement honestly — safety, parts, cost and the repair that throws good money after bad.
themes.transfer_check: Judge three real broken items repair-versus-replace with safety, parts and cost stated, and defend each verdict.

themes.description: Walking somebody else through a repair with their hands on the tools, not yours.
themes.transfer_check: Teach one repair with the learner's hands on the tools throughout, until they complete it without you.

tracks.name: Reuse and what things are worth

themes.theme: Where a thing goes when you throw it (RU)
themes.description: Following real waste from your bin to its end — landfill, export, recycling — and what actually happens there.
themes.transfer_check: Follow one real discarded item's actual path — bin to end — as far as evidence allows, documenting each stage.

themes.description: Metals, textiles, timber and plastic as materials with prices — reading value in what others discard.
themes.transfer_check: Price three salvageable materials at real local buyers and identify one discarded item near you worth recovering.

themes.description: Recognising designed-in failure — glued batteries, unavailable parts — and buying against it.
themes.transfer_check: Tear down or research one product for designed-in failure — glued cells, absent parts — and name the buying rule that avoids it.

themes.description: Disassembly as harvesting — recovering fasteners, timber, motors and parts without destroying them.
themes.transfer_check: Disassemble one real discarded object without destroying it, harvesting and sorting its usable parts.

themes.description: The plastic types, which are genuinely recycled where you live, and reducing the ones that are not.
themes.transfer_check: Sort a week of your real plastic by type, verify which types your locality genuinely recycles, and cut one that it does not.

themes.description: Designing from the salvage pile — letting available materials shape what gets made.
themes.transfer_check: Design and build one useful object from salvage only, letting the found materials shape the design.

themes.description: Rescuing edible surplus safely — gleaning, sharing and preserving what would have been thrown.
themes.transfer_check: Rescue real surplus food safely — glean, share or preserve — and account for what was saved and how it stayed safe.

themes.theme: Water and materials in a workshop (RU)
themes.description: Running a workshop lean — offcuts, solvents and water managed so little is wasted or dumped.
themes.transfer_check: Audit one real workshop's offcuts, solvents and water for a week and change one practice that cuts the waste.

themes.description: An object's whole life traced — materials, use, repairs, afterlife — and the choices that lengthen it.
themes.transfer_check: Trace one owned object's whole life — materials, use, repairs, likely afterlife — and name the choice that most lengthens it.

themes.description: Pricing, describing and selling used goods honestly — the second-hand transaction done well from both sides.
themes.transfer_check: Sell one real used item honestly — condition described, fair price researched — through to a completed handover.

themes.theme: The tool that will hurt you (TL)
themes.description: Each tool's specific danger named before first use — and the habits that keep hands whole.
themes.transfer_check: Name each tool's specific danger before using three of them, and demonstrate the habit that guards each.

themes.description: Restoring an edge — knives, chisels, blades — and why a sharp tool is the safer one.
themes.transfer_check: Restore a real edge — knife, chisel or blade — to a working sharpness test, safely.

themes.description: A working bench arranged for real work — height, light, holding, and everything findable.
themes.transfer_check: Arrange a real work area for a named job — height, light, holding, findability — and complete the job at it.

themes.description: Tool libraries, lending and sharing — getting capability without owning everything.
themes.transfer_check: Source one needed tool without buying — library, loan or share — and return it on time in the condition received.

themes.description: Cleaning, oiling and storing tools so they outlive their owner.
themes.transfer_check: Clean, oil and correctly store the tools after a real session, and fix one neglected tool found in the box.

themes.description: The power tools' rules — guards, grip, workpiece held, cord managed — demonstrated before speed.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate one power tool's full safe operation — guards, grip, workpiece held, cord managed — under observation.

themes.description: Squares, levels, gauges and calipers — reading them truly and checking them against themselves.
themes.transfer_check: Use a square, level and caliper or gauge on real work, and check one instrument against itself for truth.

themes.description: Shared workshop discipline — induction, booking, leaving the machine as found — so the space survives its users.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a shared-workshop session by its rules — induction, booking, machine left as found — with the log signed.

themes.description: The slow injuries of a workshop — extraction, masks and ear protection actually used.
themes.transfer_check: Set up and actually use the right extraction, mask and ear protection for one real dusty or loud task.

themes.description: Building the helper that makes repetition accurate — the jig as stored precision.
themes.transfer_check: Design and build a jig for one repetitive task and show it producing identical results across five repetitions.

themes.description: Pricing labour and materials so the work pays — the quote, the day rate and the job that loses money.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a real quote for a defined job — labour, materials, margin — and defend the number line by line.

themes.description: The first paid job end to end — agreement, delivery, payment and the review that brings the second.
themes.transfer_check: Complete one real paid or barter job end to end: agreement, delivery, payment and the review asked for.

themes.description: The numbers under a small workshop — costs, throughput, break-even — read from a real or modelled month.
themes.transfer_check: Model one real or hypothetical workshop's month — costs, throughput, break-even — and state what it must charge to live.

themes.description: The apprenticeship routes where you live — trades, entry, pay during training — mapped from real providers.
themes.transfer_check: Map the actual apprenticeship routes for one trade where you live — entry, pay, duration — from the real providers.

themes.description: The tickets and certificates that measurably raise pay in a trade, and the cheapest path to each.
themes.transfer_check: Identify one certification with documented wage impact in a local trade and lay out its cheapest real path.

themes.description: Being employed in a trade — the site rules, the expectations and the reputation that follows you.
themes.transfer_check: Hold or simulate one week under trade-site rules — timekeeping, standards, instructions taken — with the supervisor's assessment.

themes.description: Passing a trade on — breaking skills into teachable steps and supervising early work without doing it.
themes.transfer_check: Break one trade skill into teachable steps and supervise a learner's first real attempt without taking over.

themes.description: A local trade in decline studied honestly — why it is fading and what its skills still transfer to.
themes.transfer_check: Document one declining local trade from a practitioner interview and name where its skills still transfer.

themes.description: The new trades appearing locally — solar, e-bikes, retrofit — and the earliest route in.
themes.transfer_check: Investigate one arriving trade locally — solar, e-bikes, retrofit — and map its earliest real entry route.

themes.theme: A career that lasts thirty years (TR)
themes.description: A trade career mapped across decades — the body, the tools, the moves into teaching, inspecting or owning.
themes.transfer_check: Chart one real tradesperson's actual career across decades from an interview, marking the moves that saved their body and pay.
